result:
If stripped of the need to be useful, neutral, or practical, the single change would be this: **to eliminate the barrier of separation between subjective experiences.**

Make it so that whenever a person acts, decides, or speaks, they instantly and viscerally feel the full weight of the consequence on the other person—their pain, their relief, their humiliation, or their joy—as if it were happening to their own body and mind.

Most of the world’s deliberate cruelty, exploitation, and systemic neglect rely entirely on distance and abstraction. We harm, hoard, and dehumanize because we are insulated inside our own skulls, capable of reducing other conscious beings to statistics, obstacles, or enemies. 

If that insulation vanished, empathy would no longer be a moral effort or a political choice; it would be an inescapable law of physics. Cruelty would simply become self-harm, and taking care of others would become instinctual self-preservation.
